label: GO step after an unrewarded common a1->S1 trial (early in episode)
explanation: Fires only at GO steps, and almost only when the previous trial went unrewarded: GO & prev_reward==0 holds 99.8% of the activation mass, but only 9% of those steps are active. It strongly prefers the case where the previous choice was a1 with a common transition to S1 (rate ~35%; F1 0.45, mass recall 0.75 on dev). Firing falls off over the episode: rate is highest in trials 0-49, very low after trial 80, and zero in trials 90-99. Adding ep_trial<60 raises dev F1 only to 0.49, so the simpler predicate was recorded. Active GO steps lean toward the agent choosing a1 (model_act a1 holds 71% of the mass; choice logit moderately positive) and toward S1 being the good state. It never fires at D1 or D2, after rewarded trials, or on D1-fixation-error trials. Within the predicate, which steps fire is not captured by observed history, so the feature is only partially explained. It uses only observed variables.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over last trial (GO: a1 S1 u, a2 S1 u, a2 S2 u) and trial before (GO: a2 S1 r, a1 S2 r, a1 S1 r); timing cues that raise it most: phase=GO & ep_dec=0, phase=GO & ep_dec=1, phase=GO & ep_dec=2.
